basics.name: Khushal Hatkar
basics.label: BS-MS in Materials Science
basics.summary: Broadly interested in in-situ and operando electron microscopy and advanced characterisation for probing structure–property relationships in functional materials. My work centres on correlated oxide systems, but I am motivated by any problem where nanoscale dynamics - phase transitions, domain evolution, defect-mediated phenomena - can be resolved through TEM, electron diffraction, and spectroscopy. I also integrate computational tools (image simulation, 4D-STEM analysis, spectral processing) with experimental microscopy to extract quantitative insights.

work.name: Centre for Nanoscience Engineering (CeNSE), IISc
work.summary: Opto-Thermal Studies on VO2 Microwires Using In-Situ Raman Spectroscopy
highlights: Investigating the modulation of the metal-insulator transition (MIT) temperature in VO2 microwires through controlled nano-indentation
Performing in-situ opto-thermal experiments using Raman spectroscopy as both a probe and stimulus
Characterising nanoscale phase domain evolution during the MIT using TEM
Tools: Raman Spectroscopy, Nano-indentation, Python, COMSOL Multiphysics, SEM, TEM, XRD

work.name: Department of Materials Engineering, IISc
highlights: Performed EBSD orientation mapping to analyse texture evolution and grain boundary character distribution
Conducted complementary SEM, EDS, and WDS analyses to understand composition and gain microstructural insights

work.name: Garrett Motion
